Jose T. Cuyos Sr. II Integrated School

A formal school seal in the Philippine tradition, where every element and every count stands for something about the school.

Symbolism

Meaning, in numbers

8

Rays of the sun

A great sun settling behind the peaks, with the eight rays of the flag’s sun reaching to the rim: the light of learning, rising where the flag’s blue and red meet, split as the flag hangs vertically in peacetime (blue left, red right).

2

Mountain peaks

A far-flung school in the uplands, and its two departments, elementary and secondary, integrated into one.

1

Book-bridge

An open book is the deck of a highland hanging bridge between the two peaks: education reaches learners even in the mountains and carries them across to opportunity. Together we bridge.

4

Rice terraces

The four DepEd core values, Maka-Diyos, Maka-tao, Makakalikasan and Makabansa, built step by step like terraces in the valley the school serves.

13

Grains on each stalk

Kindergarten plus Grades 1 to 12: every level of the integrated K–12 school, carried by the palay wreath.

Construction: 8 rays at 20° intervals (±10°, ±30°, ±50°, ±70°), each reaching the rim of the medallion; woven band r 127–140, palay wreath r 157, rope r 175–193, outer rim r 243.
Anatomy of the Seal

Built like an heirloom

Gold

The gold of Rosario, its mines and its livelihood, in the sun, the wreath, the terraces and every line of the seal.

The woven band

A strip of hand-woven cloth in the red, black, white and yellow of Philippine indigenous weaving, drawn stitch by stitch: human figures with raised arms for the people and their community, stepped diamond “eyes” for protection, and sawtooth borders. It honours the school’s Indigenous Peoples learners and holds the whole scene together.

Rope & ribbon

The motto’s banner rests on a ring of twisted rope, the cable of a highland hanging bridge, holding the whole scene together.

Est. 2012

The founding year at the foot of the outer ring, the way Philippine school seals traditionally carry it.

Logo Family

One seal, three sizes of voice

Typography

Three voices, one hierarchy

Libre Baskerville

Name · Bold

A sturdy, classical serif with clear, open letters. Bold capitals for the school name around the seal; title case in the logos.

Together we bridge

Motto · Italic

The same family’s italic carries the motto on the ribbon and beside the logos: one family, two voices.

MONTSERRAT

Labels · Semibold

A quiet geometric sans, widely spaced, for “Integrated School” and “Est. 2012”.

  • Keep the seal on Deep Forest, Paper Cream or white. Never place it on photos without a solid backing.
  • Clear space around every logo: at least the diameter of the sun.
  • Minimum sizes: seal 96 px / 25 mm, medallion 48 px, mark 16 px.
  • Use the 3D seal on screens, social media and full-colour print. For embroidery, rubber stamps, engraving and one-colour print, use the flat files (*-flat.svg), which carry the same design without lighting effects.
